title: Exchange and Transport Systems
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Biology: Exchange and Transport Worksheets
standard_code: A level Biology: Organisms exchange substances with their environment
standard_text: Surface area to volume ratio, gas exchange in single-celled organisms, insects, fish, plants and humans, digestion and absorption, haemoglobin and oxygen transport, the circulatory system and the heart, tissue fluid, and transport in plants.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level biology worksheets on exchange and transport: SA:V ratio, gas exchange, ventilation, digestion, haemoglobin, cardiac output, the heart and transpiration. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate.

body_html:
How to think about it

Large organisms have a small surface area to volume ratio, so they need specialised exchange surfaces with a large area, a short diffusion distance and a steep concentration gradient. Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate; pulmonary ventilation = tidal volume × breathing rate.

Haemoglobin loads oxygen where the partial pressure is high and unloads it in respiring tissues; more CO₂ shifts the dissociation curve to the right (the Bohr effect). Water is pulled up the xylem by transpiration (cohesion–tension); sugars move in the phloem by mass flow.

Example

SV 70 cm³, HR 72. Cardiac output?

70 × 72 = 5,040 cm³ min⁻¹

Answer: 5.04 dm³ min⁻¹

Example

SA:V of a 2 cm cube?

SA = 24 cm², V = 8 cm³

Answer: 3 : 1

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to change cm³ to dm³.
  • Thinking bigger animals have a bigger SA:V.
  • Saying phloem carries water up from the roots.

faq.q: Why is the oxygen dissociation curve S-shaped?
faq.a: After one oxygen binds, haemoglobin changes shape and loads more oxygen easily (cooperative binding).
Water evaporating from leaves pulls a continuous column of water molecules, held by hydrogen bonds, up the xylem.

items.q: Why can insects not grow very large?
c: gases move along the tracheae mainly by diffusion, which is slow over long distances
items.e: Muscle movement can help ventilate the tracheae.

items.q: What is the counter-current system in fish gills?

water and blood flow the same way
water and blood flow in opposite directions, keeping a diffusion gradient along the whole lamella
items.e: More oxygen is absorbed than with parallel flow.

items.q: Why are alveoli efficient gas exchange surfaces?

items.e: Ventilation keeps a steep gradient.

items.e: The cartilage is C-shaped.

items.q: Why are gill filaments covered in lamellae?

items.e: Each lamella has many capillaries.

items.q: How is air carried to the cells of an insect?

What happens during inspiration?
c: the external intercostal muscles and diaphragm contract, so the volume of the thorax increases
items.e: Air pressure in the lungs falls below atmospheric pressure.

items.q: How do insects reduce water loss through gas exchange?

items.q: Which blood vessel brings oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
items.e: It enters the left atrium.

items.q: When do the semilunar valves open?

items.q: Why do capillaries have walls one cell thick?

items.q: Which blood vessel carries blood from the heart to the lungs?
items.e: It carries deoxygenated blood.

items.q: What is the Bohr effect?
c: a higher partial pressure of CO₂ lowers haemoglobin's affinity for oxygen
haemoglobin binds CO₂ more strongly than O₂
items.e: The dissociation curve moves to the right.

items.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker wall than the right?
c: it pumps blood to the lungs
it receives blood from the vena cava
it pumps blood all round the body at higher pressure
items.e: The right ventricle only pumps to the lungs.

items.q: Why is the oxygen dissociation curve S-shaped?
c: binding the first oxygen changes the shape and makes it easier for more to bind (cooperative binding)
items.e: The curve is steepest in the middle.

items.e: Smoking and a high-saturated-fat diet are others.

items.q: What is an atheroma?
c: a fatty deposit in an artery wall
a blood clot in a vein
items.e: It can lead to thrombosis and heart attacks.

items.q: How is tissue fluid formed?

items.q: In 2 minutes an air bubble in a potometer moves 15 mm along a capillary tube of radius 0.75 mm. Calculate the rate of water uptake in mm³ min⁻¹.
items.e: Volume = πr²d = π × 0.75² × 15 = 26.5 mm³; ÷ 2 min = 13.3 mm³ min⁻¹.

items.q: What is transpiration?
c: the loss of water vapour from the leaves through the stomata
items.e: It pulls water up the xylem.

items.q: How do radioactive tracers show translocation?
c: dye shows water in the xylem
¹⁴CO₂ is supplied to a leaf and labelled sugars are found in the phloem
items.e: Autoradiography shows the path.

items.q: In 2 minutes an air bubble in a potometer moves 36 mm along a capillary tube of radius 0.75 mm. Calculate the rate of water uptake in mm³ min⁻¹.
items.e: Volume = πr²d = π × 0.75² × 36 = 63.6 mm³; ÷ 2 min = 31.8 mm³ min⁻¹.

items.q: In 6 minutes an air bubble in a potometer moves 30 mm along a capillary tube of radius 0.60 mm. Calculate the rate of water uptake in mm³ min⁻¹.

items.q: Which factor increases the rate of transpiration?
items.e: Molecules evaporate faster.

items.q: What does a ringing experiment show?

items.e: Evidence that phloem carries organic substances.

items.q: In 6 minutes an air bubble in a potometer moves 40 mm along a capillary tube of radius 0.25 mm. Calculate the rate of water uptake in mm³ min⁻¹.

items.q: What is a source in translocation?
c: where sugars are used or stored
where sugars are made or released, such as a leaf
items.e: A sink uses or stores sugars.

items.q: What forms the xylem?
c: dead cells with no end walls, forming continuous tubes
items.e: The tubes are strengthened by lignin.

items.q: Why does high humidity reduce transpiration?
c: the water potential gradient between the leaf and the air is smaller
items.e: Less water vapour diffuses out.

items.q: Why do stomata close at night in most plants?
c: there is no light for photosynthesis, so closing reduces water loss
items.e: Guard cells lose turgor.

items.q: What are companion cells for?

items.q: What is root pressure?
